clue.text: Doctor sick of bore

parts.note: sick means ill

explanation.surface: A medic is fed up with someone tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' looks like a tiresome person, but it is the verb or noun for making a hole.
explanation.definitionFit: To drill is to make a hole with a rotating tool, the same as to bore.

clue.text: Far from well-educated under a new arrangement

indicators.note: a new arrangement says the letters of the words before it are put in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone poorly schooled is being reorganised under some new scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under a new arrangement' reads as a phrase about a scheme, but 'new arrangement' shuffles UNDER and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unread has done little reading, so is poorly educated or uninformed.

clue.text: Housing for people of mature years in principle

indicators.note: in says the grown-up people sit inside the word for principle

parts.note: a tenet is a principle or belief
grown men are adults, people of mature years

explanation.surface: In theory, there should be homes for the elderly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in principle' reads as 'theoretically', but 'in' is the container signal and 'principle' gives TENET.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenement is a block of flats, a building used for housing many households.

clue.text: The way young attendant goes around a ship

indicators.note: goes around says the page encloses the next pieces

parts.note: a page is a boy attendant
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A cabin boy walks round a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: PAGE opens after its P to take in A and SS.
explanation.definitionFit: A passage is a corridor or route, a way through somewhere.

clue.text: Last month or the present time

explanation.surface: A note about the year's end or about now.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense relies on the puzzle being published in that month.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the final month of the calendar, and the time when the puzzle appeared, mid-winter of that year.

clue.text: Can't be taken in? There's no answer to that!

explanation.surface: A remark that is both hard to swallow and unanswerable.
explanation.definitionFit: A substance that will not dissolve cannot be absorbed into a liquid; a problem with no solution has no answer.

clue.text: Irish fellow plainly much attached to an old house

definitions.text: Irish fellow plainly much attached to an old house

parts.words: Irish fellow plainly much attached to an old house
parts.note: an Ulster Protestant loyal to the royal House of William III, so a man devoted to an old dynasty

explanation.surface: An Irishman is clearly very fond of an ancient home.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'old house' is a royal dynasty, not a building: the Northern Irish loyalist order takes its name from William of that house.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Orange Order in Northern Ireland honour William III, of the Dutch royal House.

clue.text: A portion of prunes is chosen, naturally, as a laxative

indicators.note: a portion of says the letters run across the words that follow

explanation.surface: Some prunes are picked as a natural remedy for constipation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prunes' plants the idea of a laxative but gives no letters; the run is in 'chosen, naturally'.
explanation.definitionFit: Senna is a plant extract used as a purgative medicine.

clue.text: Collection of horses for the boss

explanation.surface: Horses kept for breeding, owned by the employer.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud is a breeding establishment of horses, and also a raised knob or ornament, which is a boss.

clue.text: They give their support to British lines — and others

definitions.text: They give their support to British lines — and others

parts.words: They give their support to British lines — and others
parts.note: railway beams under the track, and also people asleep or undercover agents

explanation.surface: Some people back British policy, and so do others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'British lines' are railway tracks; in Britain the cross-beams holding rails are so named.
explanation.definitionFit: Railway cross-ties support rails; the same word covers sleeping people and dormant spies.

clue.text: A man has little alternative after turning "green"

indicators.note: after puts the alternative behind the turned word
turning says the word for green is read backwards

parts.note: vert is the heraldic word for green
or is the short word offering an alternative

explanation.surface: A man has small choice after becoming environmentally minded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning green' suggests going eco, but 'turning' turns VERT round to give TREV.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a common male first name, so any man could be called that.

clue.text: Sums up sound woodworking tools

definitions.note: plural here while the answer is singular; the setter treats the tool name loosely

indicators.note: sound says the word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: sums up means adds

explanation.surface: A tally of the noise made by carpentry equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is plural but the answer names one such tool.
explanation.definitionFit: An adze is a cutting tool with an arched blade set at right angles to the handle, used for shaping timber.

clue.text: He'll flit around, showing a light touch in disorder

indicators.note: in places the light touch inside the word for a disorder

parts.note: gout is a painful joint disorder
a dab is a light touch

explanation.surface: Someone flits about with a deft hand amid chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in disorder' looks like an anagram signal, but GOUT is the disorder that holds A DAB.
explanation.definitionFit: A gadabout is a person who restlessly goes from place to place seeking amusement.

clue.text: Restriction the country's to bring back

parts.note: a rein is a check or restriction
a state is a country; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: Bringing back a nation's restrictions.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinstate is to restore someone or something to a former position.

clue.text: Confidential information put about within cliques

indicators.note: within puts the word for about inside the cliques

parts.note: sects are factions or cliques
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Private knowledge circulates in exclusive groups.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put about' suggests spreading gossip, but 'about' gives RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Secrets are matters kept private, confidential knowledge.

clue.text: A writer — heartless rogue, and stout

indicators.note: heartless says the inner letters of the word for rogue are removed, leaving its first and last letters

parts.note: porter is a dark beer like stout

explanation.surface: A writer described as a rogue without a heart, and fat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stout' looks like a description of the writer, but it is the beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A reporter is a journalist who writes news stories.

clue.text: Rats let loose can cause alarm

indicators.note: let loose says the letters are set free to form a new order

explanation.surface: Rodents running free can frighten people.
explanation.definitionFit: To startle is to give someone a sudden shock or fright.

clue.text: Debate, cast vote, and lark about

indicators.note: cast suggests the letters of vote are thrown into a new order
about suggests the letters of lark are moved around

explanation.surface: An argument, a vote taken, and some fooling around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast vote' reads as voting, but 'cast' and 'about' together shuffle the letters of VOTE and LARK.
explanation.definitionFit: To talk over a matter is to discuss or debate it.

clue.text: Plug organised sport, including fitness training

indicators.note: including says the jumbled sport letters hold the training piece
organised says the letters of sport are put in order afresh

parts.note: PE is physical education

explanation.surface: Promote organised games with exercise classes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' shuffles SPORT into STOPR, and 'including' puts PE inside after STOP.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopper is a bung or plug for closing a bottle or hole.

clue.text: Encourage to get in alcoholic drink

parts.note: spirit is distilled alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: Urging someone to buy strong liquor.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspirit is to fill with courage or animate.

clue.text: Sat on the staff over a certain point

indicators.note: in a down clue over puts the staff above the point

parts.note: a rod is a staff or stick
E is east, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone sat on a stick above a particular spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sat on' means mounted, as a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: If you rode a horse, you sat on it and travelled.

clue.text: The bar backed this perjurer

indicators.note: backed says the word for bar is read backwards

parts.note: a rail is a bar

explanation.surface: The legal profession supported this false witness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The bar' suggests barristers, but it is just a rail.
explanation.definitionFit: A perjurer tells untruths under oath, so is someone who lies.

clue.text: Give the impression of being a very quiet listener

parts.note: pp is pianissimo, the musical mark for very quiet
an ear is what listens

explanation.surface: Seem to be someone who hears softly.
explanation.definitionFit: To appear to be something is to seem so.

clue.text: A rod for fresh-water fish

explanation.surface: A fishing rod for river fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A perch is an old unit of length equal to a rod or pole, and also a freshwater fish.

clue.text: Sorted out and kept in reserve

indicators.note: out says the letters of sorted are put out of order

explanation.surface: Things organised and set aside for later.
explanation.definitionFit: Things stored are put away for future use.

clue.text: A jogger when others are playing

definitions.text: A jogger when others are playing

parts.words: A jogger when others are playing
parts.note: someone who jogs memories in the theatre wings while the actors perform, not a runner

explanation.surface: A runner goes out while the rest are at their games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jogger' suggests running; here it jogs the memory of actors in a play.
explanation.definitionFit: In the theatre this person supplies forgotten lines to actors during a performance.

clue.text: Pronounce complete

explanation.definitionFit: To utter is to speak or voice, and utter as an adjective means total or absolute.

clue.text: Application of lace — never ruffled

indicators.note: ruffled says the letters are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: Using lace that has never been frilled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Application' suggests applying lace; here it means pertinence.
explanation.definitionFit: Relevance is how well something applies to the matter in hand, its application.
